title: A hierarchy for a diverse dataset
paper: MerMED-FM: Multimodal, Multi-Disease Medical Imaging Foundation Model
citation: Zhou et al. · The Lancet Digital Health · 2026
image_alt: Hierarchical circular dataset-composition chart adapted from MerMED-FM
lesson: Group individual datasets within modalities so readers can see both the collection's breadth and its composition.
note: Uses the tutorial's approximate, image-derived counts. This adapts the design; it does not reproduce MerMED-FM's dataset statistics. Repeated datasets are not deduplicated.
credit: Source figure: Zhou et al. Adaptation: VCMI tutorial.

title: Many datasets, one circular overview
paper: An explainable biomedical foundation model via large-scale concept-enhanced vision–language pretraining
citation: Nie et al. · Nature Biomedical Engineering · 2026
image_alt: Circular bar-chart reconstruction grouped by task and modality
lesson: Use consistent grouping and a clear hierarchy to organize a large number of dataset labels.
note: Counts are estimated from measured bar radii using a logarithmic calibration. These are approximate visual reconstructions, not verified source statistics. The script also offers a horizontal layout.
credit: Source figure: Nie et al. Reconstruction: VCMI tutorial.

title: Make the change in ordering visible
paper: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
image_alt: Base and reinforcement-learning model pass-at-k curves with crossover markers
lesson: Annotate the crossover when the scientific question concerns how the relative ordering changes with the sampling budget.
note: The markers interpolate between supplied points in log(k). They are visual estimates, not independently measured thresholds. The before image is a tutorial plot, not an original paper figure.
credit: Research reference: Yue et al. Plot and refinement: VCMI tutorial.

title: Show the gain without mental arithmetic
paper: CancerVerse: A Fully Open Longitudinal and Multimodal Dataset for Multicancer Screening
image_alt: Segmentation bars annotated with percentage-point gains and a radiologist agreement reference
lesson: Label absolute gains directly and explain contextual reference lines so readers can assess the intended comparison.
note: The 62.2% inter-annotator agreement comes from a smaller subset. The model's score on that subset is 50.8%; the four bars summarize the full test set. The cropped bar axis follows the source design and exaggerates visible length differences; consider a dot plot or zero-based bars for a new figure.
dependencies: Python, Matplotlib; values embedded in the script
credit: Research and Figure 3a reference: Li et al. Reconstruction: VCMI tutorial.
